prompts.name: check_setup
prompts.title: Check CapMonster setup
prompts.description: Check that CapMonster and the browser work before solving a captcha
prompts.template:
Check that CapMonster is ready to use. Run each check yourself, then report one pass/fail line per check and, for every failure, what to fix. Do not start solving anything.

1. capmonster server: call get_supported_tasks and get_balance. Report how many task types are supported and the balance. An error about a missing key means CAPMONSTER_API_KEY is not set in this MCP server's environment.
2. Docs access: call get_docs for https://docs.capmonster.cloud/llms.txt and confirm it returns content.
3. Browser (needed only to analyze live pages; skip it if I only want CapMonster integrated into code): with the patchright server, open https://example.com (browser_navigate) and confirm a page snapshot comes back.

If a check fails, stop and tell me what is wrong instead of continuing.

prompts.name: solve_captcha
prompts.title: Solve a captcha on a page
prompts.description: Solve a captcha on a web page: identify it, get a token from CapMonster, inject it and verify

arguments.name: url
arguments.description: Address of the page with the captcha

arguments.name: how_it_appears
arguments.description: When the captcha shows up: right away, after a click, after login...
arguments.default: not specified: find out from the page, and ask me if a login or a click is needed

arguments.name: hints
arguments.description: Optional hints: proxy to use, region, anything that blocks the page

prompts.name: integrate_into_project
prompts.title: Add CapMonster to my project
prompts.description: Put a working CapMonster captcha solve into my project's code with the official SDK

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Language of the project, if it is not obvious

arguments.name: module_path
arguments.description: File or module where the code should go
arguments.default: pick a fitting place in the project and tell me where
